page: Amazon Web Services m8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-hypervised virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz with one thread per core. The processor features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as VAES and SHA-NI.

The system is provisioned with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs bundled into this instance tier.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread capabilities and robust compute density. The m8a.4xlarge ranks in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 2835.0, a stress-ng score of 3778.48, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21874.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 106.87 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 67.9 GB/sec for large uncached writes. Data compression throughput is notable, reaching 41.42 GB/sec on single-threaded gzip and 278.84 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Without local NVMe drives, storage-heavy operations must rely on external network-attached storage, placing high dependency on the 8 Gbps network link. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the non-hyperthreaded physical cores and high single-thread throughput maximize compute value for per-core licensed software. The instance is well suited for enterprise application backends, container orchestration, static web servers, CI/CD runners, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 16-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with dedicated allocation, clocked at 4.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, each vCPU corresponds directly to a physical core with one thread per core. It is paired with 64.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature GPUs, operating with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight exceptional single-thread performance, placing in the top 10% in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, alongside strong compression and static web serving speeds of 54.7 GB/sec. The instance delivers solid resource efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated core performance without hyperthreading contention, making it suitable for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, application middleware, and small-model CPU inference.
